citation.title: Ion heat transport dynamics during edge localized mode cycles at ASDEX Upgrade
citation.authors: E. Viezzer, M. Cavedon, E. Fable, F.M. Laggner, R.M. McDermott, et al.; ASDEX Upgrade Team; EUROfusion MST1 Team
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1741-4326/aaa22f (this paper's own DOI, PDF p2 header; distinct from DOIs of cited works)

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1-10 (PDF p1 cover; journal p1-9 = PDF p2-10), incl. Figs 1-7
scope_read.limitations: Figure values were read visually only. Ref [26] (Ti/Te recovery comparison) and ref [19] (spectrometer) were not read.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Edge/pedestal Ti changes and recovers within a few ms around type-I ELMs.
claim_checks.source_finding: In an ELM-synchronized AUG D discharge (~85 Hz ELMs), separatrix Ti first rose at ELM onset and then the whole edge profile dropped. The pre-ELM profile recovered 3-4 ms after the crash, versus 60 ms energy confinement time. A single ELM in a He plasma showed a similar 3-4 ms recovery.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p6, Sec 5.1, Fig 5; PDF p8, Sec 5.2, Fig 7
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On ASDEX Upgrade, edge ion temperature measured with sub-ms charge-exchange spectroscopy has been reported to collapse and recover within roughly 3-4 ms of type-I ELM crashes [Viezzer2018].
claim_checks.qualification: Results come from AUG, specific discharges, and the edge region (rho_pol 0.95-1.0). The D case is coherently averaged over ELMs. Separatrix uncertainties are large (PDF p6-7). This is not KSTAR, carbon CES, or a pedestal-top chord. The 3-4 ms scale is below the study's 10 ms grid, so do not imply that the nowcast resolves intra-ELM dynamics.

claim_checks.source_finding: A fast edge CXRS spectrometer (up to 9 lines of sight) can run at 50 us integration but requires impurity seeding; standard edge systems run at 2.3 ms. The D case used He2+ at 65 us, rebinned to 100 us; the He case used 100 us, rebinned to 250 us. Ti is approximated by impurity temperature.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p3, Sec 2; PDF p5-6, Sec 5.1; PDF p7, Sec 5.2
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Dedicated fast CXRS configurations with impurity seeding have resolved edge Ti on tens-of-microseconds integration times, compared with ms-scale standard systems [Viezzer2018].
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to a dedicated, seeded, limited-chord configuration. It was used offline, not in real time.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Ms-scale Ti dynamics motivate causal nowcasting of reported CES temperature.
claim_checks.source_finding: The paper is offline interpretive/predictive ASTRA transport analysis. It addresses no estimators, nowcasting, BES/ECEI inputs, or report latency.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p4, Sec 3; PDF p9, Sec 6
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Because pedestal Ti can evolve faster than typical CES reporting intervals, it is useful to ask whether a causal estimate of the current report can be formed from other fast diagnostics.
claim_checks.qualification: This framing motivation is ours, not the source's. Do not cite the source as endorsing nowcasting.

input_target_timing.inputs: not_applicable (not an estimator paper). Transport inputs: ne, Te, Ti, Zeff, Prad, and sources into ASTRA (PDF p4, Sec 3).
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Offline, ELM-synchronized and interpolated analysis (PDF p6)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Measured impurity Ti is taken as a proxy for main-ion Ti, justified by fast equilibration (PDF p5). In He, main-ion and N temperatures roughly agree (PDF p7-8, Fig 6c).

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Spectrometer integration/rebinning times and the 100 us equilibrium mapping
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Any real-time processing, latency, or deployment
runtime_or_deployment.locator: PDF p3, Sec 2; PDF p6, Sec 5.1

forbidden_inferences: KSTAR or carbon-CES pedestal-top Ti behaves identically
The source supports or performs nowcasting or causal estimation
Our 10 ms grid resolves ELM crash dynamics
Neoclassical inter-ELM chi_i implies a physical mechanism for our estimator
The Ti-vs-Te recovery (4 vs 7-8 ms) is demonstrated here; it is attributed to ref [26] (PDF p5)
competing_or_complementary: Complementary physics context on edge Ti time scales. It is not a competing estimator.
